Well, I would like to go back to the beginning, to the question of power. We have just heard about the injustices that exist in the economic and the financial system and the request for a reform of international financial architecture that we are being— making very strongly in the Pact for the Future. And to show how inequality is embedded in the present system of multilateralism and one of the reasons why we need the reform of that multilateralism is to look, for instance, the way the so-called Special Drawing Rights are distributed. When there is a crisis like the crisis of the COVID Special Drawing Rights were distributed by the IMF proportionally to the quotas, and the quotas are such that the most rich countries have the biggest quotas and even the emerging economies have quotas that are much smaller than their present weight in the global economy. And so in a moment in which wealth was necessary to be created and distributed, it was distributed essentially to the rich. This shows how embedded is injustice in our system. And so the fight for inequality is a central aspect in— to give credibility to multilateral institutions. And then I would remind you all of the two existential challenges that we face and say that we are totally mobilized to fight in order to guarantee that we preserve humankind and we preserve the planet. We are witnessing a transfer of power that has no parallel in history. This time is not power from one state to another, from one government to another, or from governments to other sectors of society. It is a power that has been moving from governments— governments of the inclusive, the most powerful countries in the world,, but their power is being moved to a number of— a very small number of companies that tend to concentrate all the information and all the capacity to influence things. And we absolutely need to preserve— to preserve institutions that guarantee that democratic values can prevail and at the same time that human agency is never put aside in decisions that are essential for our future. I had the occasion a few days ago to condemn the robo-killers, but beyond what we see in the— I mean, battlefields, I think that we need to be aware that we are becoming more and more controlled by a small number of companies and we need to fight in order to make sure that human agency prevails and that things are not done against humanity but for the future of humanity. And this battle is far from being won as the battle for climate change is far from being won. And we have two existential battles for which multilateral institutions would need to be much more powerful than what they are now.
